column3: Literal statement omits dimension, operator and norm quantifiers. Counterexample existence may report a public result; primary passage needed before any certificate design.
Every eventual additive basis must have unbounded representation count; a finite set cannot address the infinite quantifier. No full-scope construction or unboundedness mechanism identified.
Uniform quadratic growth and arbitrary divergent g are distinct strengths. Density averaging gives constant lower bounds only, not the required divergent limsup.
All real slopes and asymptotic constant pi/sqrt(3) are essential. Row occupancy gives only 2n; finite grids do not bridge a strict asymptotic improvement.
A 99-vertex adjacency certificate would be small to check, but finding it or proving nonexistence requires global strongly regular constraints; no tractable search reduction supplied.
An extra factorial square is a finite certificate, but no candidate beyond 4,5,7 is available. Congruence checks at finite n cannot exclude all n.
Optimality needs an attaining threefold or a sharp infimum construction with singularity control, not merely the quoted lower bound. Large birational dependency burden.
Uniform signed half-power Liouville sum cannot be justified by the quoted finite check. No certified positive witness or global analytic sign argument available.
Good partition definition is external. Counting occurrences of 00 without its admissibility conditions would not test the quantified statement.
Three fixed moduli allow automaton certificates in principle, but all n requires reachable-state closure, not a prefix. Source and successor automata not inspected; no small state bound established.
Counting all isomorphism classes for every prime requires classification plus Beauville predicates. Testing p=5 would be an instance, not the asserted p+10 formula.

Primary v3 Conjecture4 and carry-transition definitions inspected. Pivot-preserving graph isomorphism is stronger than unlabelled digraph equivalence; uniform reachability/pruning remains unproved and successors unread.
Equality in an unnamed proposition supplies no literal numerical formula. Primary proposition and restricted-sum definitions are needed before testing n>=11.
Need r-arithmetic triples for each r, with arithmeticity controlled exactly; enumeration through r=15 gives no parametric family. No full-scope route.
An infinite 3-adic coefficient bound depends on external basis and regulator definitions. Finite coefficient checks do not provide a tail valuation estimate.
Cube face lattice and normalized volume are separate obligations for every n. A handful of vertex hulls cannot establish both; no explicit uniform facet model obtained.
Rank-three Ulrich existence in every odd degree needs a uniform bundle or exact determinant construction; checks to degree43 do not yield it. Geometric dependencies substantial.
Strict decrease at every nonexceptional cardinality is a global spherical packing statement. A parameter instance or correcting exceptional wording earns no credit.

Both arithmetic progressions and prime-power moduli require full generating-function or modular-form certificates. Finite moment residues are not a proof; no short source-verified modular identity identified.

Primary v1 Section5 cardinality formula, Lemma19 and Conjecture5 inspected. Exact k=2..20 checks agree, but no uniform binomial inequality or successor-body clearance established; stop before proof investment.
Existence for every even order requires a uniform Williamson construction, stronger than the reported range<=70. No construction covering the missing infinite orders.
Two Catalan polynomials require their precise definitions. Divisibility alone would not prove nonnegative quotient coefficients; no equivalence with accepted q-Motzkin helpers presumed.
Universal Sylvester coloring needs the exact local coloring map at each vertex, not just ordinary edge colors. No reduction to a known coloring theorem or finite counterexample supplied.
Order-dependent complex root bound needs uniform subtree coefficient control sharper than a fixed-radius estimate. Small-tree enumeration cannot certify all orders.
Functions g2 and g3 are defined externally; no honest inequality calculation is possible from these names alone. Primary definitions needed.

Five finite Ramsey cases could admit certificates but orders up to37 demand exhaustive obstruction coverage; no compact symmetry or structural certificate available. Large unstructured search stopped.

Strict parity excess for every Frobenius number needs a parity-changing injection with unmatched survivors, not the initial table. Endpoint conventions for trivial semigroup must be checked; no such injection found.
Genus-wide odd-type dominance needs a uniform involution/injection respecting genus. Empty-genus convention could change literal wording only; not an eligible correction.
Series F_K and coefficient normalization are external; Laurentness for every fibered knot needs a uniform finiteness argument, not polynomial fits for small knots.
Literal text itself reports the classical Leher counterexample at17*29*41; height notation also contains a stray4. Do not claim new refutation; primary body not independently audited here.
Setting two variables to1 gives n=2zw+z+w+2, hence a divisor condition on2n-3, which does not cover all integers. No finite covering of the full threshold tail established.
Alpha(n) is not precisely defined and the final sign split is empirical. First residue classes alone would be partial; no full quantified target before primary definition repair.
All powers of every permitted odd a require a uniform discrepancy identity. k=0 and a=1 conventions must be source checked; endpoint corrections are not new outcomes.
Primary v1 Conjecture10.3 and Fishburn forbidden bivincular pattern inspected. Exhaustive n<=7 counts agree; no all-n bijection/recurrence or closest successor-body clearance.
Primary v1 Conjecture10.8 gives all n>=1 formula. Exact counts1,2,5,11,21,36,57 match through7; cubic sequence fitting is not a structural enumeration or novelty clearance.
Every consecutive-prime-square interval containing a twin pair implies infinitely many twin primes. Probability and a finite sieve are insufficient for the quantified infinite claim.
Monotonicity from82 needs uniform character-zero counts and comparison over partitions; asymptotic tendency alone does not imply adjacent monotonicity. No effective recurrence bound identified.
Writing x=exp(s),y=exp(t) asks midpoint convexity of log pi(exp(2s)); prime-counting jumps obstruct naive PNT differentiation. PNT error bounds do not settle arbitrarily close x,y uniformly.
Auxiliary N(0,n) definition missing from literal record. Rank symmetry alone does not compare the claimed difference to half this external count.
Literal statement reports its own public confirmation. No new proof credit; primary theorem body and exact threshold not independently inspected here.
Almost-all Hua-type results cannot remove every exceptional N above24476. No complete covering congruence or bounded counterexample available.
General simple drawings need planar cycles and all vertices on one side for every k. Convex drawings and n<=10 do not transfer to arbitrary rotation systems.

561=3*11*17 satisfies a^561=a mod561 for every integer a; all561 residues checked exactly. Classical Carmichael phenomenon defeats literal converse; AGP attribution confuses existence with primality. No discovery credit.

Infinitely many n must satisfy all backward k, not finitely many offsets. For k>=log2(n) the bound is automatic, but the increasing small-k window still needs prime-factor control; no uniform construction.
Arbor and polytope definitions external; real roots of Ehrhart polynomial and of h* are different objects. No inference from wording alone; primary body needed.
Every finite graph requires proper neighbor-sum labeling with chi(G) labels. Polynomial-method bounds with larger palettes do not give the requested bound; no small witness or full construction.

Starting from an isolating set leaves independent vertices outside its closed neighborhood, but adding vertices one by one need not cost at most another isolating-set size. No charging argument covering all cubic graphs.
Absolute partial-sum bound for every real x>=3078 is not proved by the stated very large finite verification. Dyadic jumps from powers of2 need global cancellation; no full route.
Relevant real crossing and thermodynamic strip limit require source definitions. Transfer matrices at listed widths do not prove all3p+-1 widths.
Uniform degree identity for every nontrivial companion requires both upper bound and noncancellation lower bound under Whitehead doubling. <=11-crossing evidence does not address all knots.
